extracted.intended_audience: Students in AoPS Online courses (grades ~5-12), and their parents/instructors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and grading rules for 'writing problems' in AoPS online courses: how to prepare, attach, save, and submit full written solutions (including diagrams or LaTeX/Asymptote) and how they will be evaluated by graders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical scores range from 0 to 7. This score is primarily about whether all of the right pieces of a proof are presented—that means that all important steps are shown and fully explained, and that the explanation was properly rigorous relative to the level of the course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A score of 7 means that the solution was completely correct and well-explained, and as a result, demonstrated a solid understanding of the concepts and problem-solving strategies used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Style scores are on a scale of 0.0 - 1.0, with intermediate scores given in tenths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The types of things looked for in Style include motivation for your arguments, steps that flow in a logical order, clearly defining variables, including a diagram when needed, using consistent notation, and the other elements that make a solution, not just an answer or sequence of calculations. Style can also reflect 'elegance' or 'simplicity'—whether a clever insight minimized computations versus bashing out calculations. Punctuation, grammar, and spacing should not hinder the reader's understanding. In Intermediate or Advanced courses, elegance/simplicity may carry additional weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Feedback from Grader and Instructor
rubrics_metrics.description: Graded writing problems receive personal written feedback from an AoPS grader and your instructor, who will comment on the content as well as the style of your writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback will include tips for improvement; after reading feedback, students are encouraged to apply suggestions going forward and reflect on what parts of the solution were best. Students will be emailed when their assignment has been graded, typically within a week of the due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and Completeness of Explanation (write for a peer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write as though the person reading is one of your classmates who has not seen the problem before. Include any important observations and explain why you are doing anything that isn't totally obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guidance is a core part of producing a good solution: provide motivation, make steps flow logically, and define variables so a peer unfamiliar with the problem can follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typesetting and Use of LaTeX/Asymptote (not graded)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can include LaTeX-typeset math expressions and Asymptote graphics, but typesetting is never required and will never be a part of your grade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LaTeX expressions may be wrapped in dollar signs (e.g., $x-4=10$). Asymptote code should be placed between [asy] and [/asy] tags. Using LaTeX/Asy well does not substitute for clear exposition, and plain-text or hand-drawn diagrams are fully acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachments and Images Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If a diagram or hand-written work helps, include it by taking a picture or scanning and attaching it to your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To attach files, click 'Attach a File' and drag files or select them. Verify previews or file names appear; if a file is too large it may fail to attach. Use the 'Remove file' link to delete, and 'Done' when finished. Check the 'Attachments' heading below the response box to ensure intended files are present. If you need help resizing files, ask on the message board. Include some text in the response box (e.g., 'See attached.') to ensure the submission will be collected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving Work and What Gets Graded
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing problem homework is collected between the due date and the following day. The system collects and grades what was written the last time you clicked the SAVE button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auto-saved data is stored but not used for grading; only the manually saved version is graded. The system also auto-saves in case of outages and will ask you which version to keep if you sign back in. Students are encouraged to click SAVE often to avoid losing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Timing and Extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing problem solutions cannot be submitted earlier than the due date. Submissions will be collected after 11:59:59 PM on the due date in your time zone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need more time, you can submit an extension request (details available on the referenced extensions page). The site encourages using all available time up to the due date to think, write, and edit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auto-Graded Writing Problems (operational difference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some classes have auto-graded writing problems which are not graded by humans. These commonly appear in Calculus and programming classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auto-graded problems still ask for a complete solution; you can submit once and will be shown the full solution after completing the problem. Your response will not receive human feedback, but you will receive points for submitting. If you request a grade at the end of the course, instructors will take a closer look at these solutions when determining a grade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Model Solutions and Continued Learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Every problem in the course has a full solution you can view as soon as you have completed the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students are encouraged to read model solutions carefully as examples of well-written solutions and to read grader comments to improve future writing.
